subject: Procurement questions: payment path, marketplace credits, and invoice routing
messages:
From: Rachel Souza <rachel.souza@brightleafhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procureops@brightleafhealth.com
Date: 2028-01-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Buying flow questions — marketplace vs direct (credits / tax / invoice)

Hi Markus / Laura,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here at Brightleaf had a few follow-ups before we can move forward — apologies for the long list but want to get clarity so we can scope the onboarding timeline with Finance. High-level: we need to decide whether to route the purchase through a cloud marketplace listing (AWS/Azure/GCP) or do a direct purchase under a signed MSA + PO. Specific questions:

- If we buy via AWS Marketplace private offer, will Redwood be able to issue an invoice that follows our Net-60 PO process, or will billing always come through AWS billing and require net terms there?
- How do marketplace credits / promotional discounts interact with co-sell credits? Do credits reduce the list price used for co-sell calculations?
- Any differences across cloud marketplaces for tax handling (sales tax / VAT) we should plan for? Brightleaf has US operations + a small EU entity.
- What documents do you need from us to enable a directed-invoice private offer vs listing? (W9, SOW, vendor onboarding docs)

We prefer to close before our fiscal cut-off on 2/7 — if there is a path that guarantees delivery by then, please outline steps & timing. I attached a brief roadmap and a PO stub that Procurement provided.

Thanks,
Rachel
Rachel Souza
Head of Procurement, Brightleaf Health
procurement: 415-555-0192

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Buying flow questions — marketplace vs direct (credits / tax / invoice)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear list. Short answer up-front and then a recommended path.

Summary:
- Speed: Marketplace private offers (AWS Private Offer / Azure Private Marketplace / GCP Marketplace private) can be fastest to provision if the marketplace listing and offer setup are already in place — typically 3–10 business days for the private offer set-up itself.
- Invoice control & net terms: If you need Redwood to issue a vendor invoice with Net-60 under your PO number, the most robust path is a directed invoice via a Private Offer + Seller-of-Record configuration (we can set Redwood as seller-of-record or leverage a reseller partner). Standard marketplace billing often flows through the cloud provider which enforces their billing cadence and may not support your Net-60 terms.
- Marketplace credits vs co-sell credits: Promotional credits applied by the marketplace typically reduce the charged amount but do not change the upstream list price used for co-sell attribution in most cases — however, co-sell programs vary by vendor and may treat private-offer discounts differently. We'll coordinate with GTM so co-sell crediting isn't materially affected.
- Tax differences: AWS/Azure/GCP handle tax differently by region. For US-only purchases with Redwood issuing the invoice, you should get a Redwood invoice with the applicable US sales tax (we will require your tax jurisdiction and resale certificates if applicable). For EU entities, VAT handling depends on whether the invoice is issued by Redwood or the marketplace; we'll capture your EU VAT ID when onboarding.

Recommended path for your Net-60 requirement and 2/7 timeline:
1) Option A (preferred): Private Offer + Directed Invoice (Redwood issues invoice). We collect W9, signed SOW, and the PO. Timeline: 5–12 business days to issue Private Offer + complete vendor onboarding and generate an invoice.
2) Option B (fallback): Marketplace purchase via provider with your finance team accepting provider invoices. Timeline: fastest to provision (2–5 business days) but may break Net-60 flow and complicate co-sell credits.

Next steps I recommend we do today:
- Laura (cc) will send the Private Offer template and a short checklist of vendor onboarding items.
- Rachel — can you confirm the legal entity for billing (Brightleaf US or EU) and share any reseller or tax exemption docs?
- If you want us to draft a private-offer with invoice terms, confirm the target SKUs and the quote (we'll convert to private-offer pricing).

I've attached a draft of our marketplace terms to this thread for your legal review. Happy to hop on a 30-min call with Procurement & Legal to walk through the path.

— Markus Klein
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai | +1 650-555-0123

+1 to Markus' summary — a couple operational notes from GTM & CS: 

- Co-sell credit timing: Marketplace private offers can front-load co-sell attribution faster (once offer is accepted), but revenue recognition for partner credits follows our partner agreement. If Brightleaf needs credits applied to your invoices for accounting, confirm that with your finance team and we'll route to our partner channels where necessary.
- Reseller vs Seller-of-Record: If Procurement requires vendor onboarding that blocks marketplace vendor acceptance, we can use an approved reseller (this adds one extra week typically).
- PO validation: To avoid activation delays, please put "Redwood Inference — Private Offer" in the PO notes and include the billing entity and remit-to info.

I'll be available for a call tomorrow 10–11am PT to align on adoption milestones.

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Procurement Ops <procureops@brightleafhealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-01-19T14:06:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Buying flow questions — marketplace vs direct (credits / tax / invoice)

Markus / team — quick clarifications from Brightleaf Finance: 

- Our finance stack requires vendor invoices from the vendor (not the cloud provider) to accept Net-60. The provider invoices cannot be integrated into our AP system for Net terms.
- We cannot accept reseller intermediated invoices that change the legal vendor name unless the reseller will accept 90-day vendor onboarding timelines — that will push us past 2/7.
- For EU VAT: our EU entity has a VAT ID and prefers to be billed directly for EU-based consumption.

Given the above, we need Redwood to be the invoicing party for the US side at a minimum. Is there a way to get a Private Offer configured where Redwood is the seller-of-record and issues a Redwood invoice with Net-60? If that is not possible for AWS, what is the shortest path to satisfy our Net-60 requirement?

Thanks — attaching PO stub for reference.

Attachments: Brightleaf_PO_stub.pdf

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Rachel Souza <rachel.souza@brightleafhealth.com>, procureops@brightleafhealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, Luis Ramos <luis.ramos@procurelaw.com>

Subject: Re: Buying flow questions — marketplace vs direct (credits / tax / invoice)

Thanks for the clarity — that helps a lot. Actionable plan below so we can hit your 2/7 cut-off if possible.

Planned approach: Private Offer + Redwood-issued Invoice (seller-of-record)
- Requirement list from Brightleaf: W9 (US entity), signed SOW / statement of work, PO with the billing entity noted.
- Redwood actions: put a Private Offer in place for the agreed SKUs, set Redwood as seller-of-record for the US invoice, and generate an initial invoice tied to your PO.
- Timeline: 7–12 business days once we have the W9, signed SOW, and confirmed SKUs. If Brightleaf can sign the SOW and return the W9 today, we'll aim for 7 business days.
- Co-sell / credits: We'll document the gross list price in the private-offer record so co-sell compensation can be processed separately; credits/promos applied at checkout will not alter the co-sell reference price. We'll coordinate with your GTM contact to confirm the crediting flow.
- EU billing: For any EU invoicing, please send the EU VAT ID and preferred billed entity; if Redwood issues EU invoices we will include VAT handling accordingly.

Immediate next steps:
1) Rachel / Procurement: Attach W9 and confirm billed entity for US invoices.
2) Laura: I'll need help creating the private-offer record and a DocuSign envelope for the SOW. Laura, can you produce the DocuSign link by EOD 1/22?
3) Rachel: please confirm the SKUs you want included (I can draft a quote).

If the Private Offer path stalls, fallback is a direct MSA + Redwood invoice (no marketplace) — that path supports Net-60 but usually takes longer to set up from a contracting perspective.

I'll set a 30-min alignment for Thursday 1/25 with Finance + Legal + Redwood GTM unless you prefer earlier.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Channel Partnerships | Redwood Inference
